1. Verify current-bill arithmetic: confirm meter reads (70,731 − 69,989) imply 742 kWh, line items ($18.38 + $19.52 + $99.73) sum to $137.63, and compute the observed change versus last month ($137.63 − $117.22 = +$20.41). Treat any internal mismatch as a potential billing error.

2. Confirm both billing periods fall under the same AEP Ohio RS tariff (fixed $18.38/month; first-tier variable $0.0263125 + $0.13441 = $0.1607225 per kWh). Since rates are unchanged, set price_usd = $0.00. Since both periods are 31 days and the customer charge is a flat monthly fee while energy/riders are billed per kWh, set days_usd = $0.00.

3. Estimate weather_usd: use the NOAA bill history to derive a weather-to-usage relationship for the cooling season, isolate the weather-attributable kWh difference between last month (CDD 53.5, HDD 137) and the current period (CDD 214.5, HDD 49), and value those weather-driven kWh at the effective variable rate (~$0.1607/kWh).

4. Compute usage_usd as the residual so that price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals exactly +$20.41 (equivalently, value the non-weather portion of the 127 kWh increase at the variable rate).

5. Screen for a billing error by comparing billed kWh to meter reads, line-item sums to the total, and tariff-modeled charges to the actual total; set billing_error_suspected and billing_error_usd accordingly (expected: false / null, allowing only normal rounding).

6. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
